newsitem.title: USA: EIA sees 1st qtr US distillate use at 3.72 mln bpd.
newsitem.headline: EIA sees 1st qtr US distillate use at 3.72 mln bpd.

text.p: U.S. demand for distillate should reach 3.72 million barrels per day in the first quarter of 1997, 130,000 bpd more than previously expected, the Energy Information Administration said Friday.
The 3.6 percent increase reflected a surge in demand for diesel in transportation which was expected to continue from the last quarter of 1996, EIA said in its latest "Short-Term Energy Outlook".
EIA boosted its forecast for distillate production, including diesel and heating oil, for the first quarter of 1997 by 70,000 bpd to 3.22 million bpd, to meet the demand.
Higher crude oil prices than earlier projected were expected push U.S. retail heating oil prices in the first three months of 1997 to $1.06 per gallon, up 5 cents from EIA's previous outlook.
Retail heating oil prices in the last quarter of 1996 at an average $1.05 per gallon were 3 cents higher than EIA had projected because of soaring crude prices and strong demand.
U.S. demand for distillate in the fourth quarter of 1996 climbed to 3.5 million bpd, 5 percent more than EIA projected three months ago.
Colder weather than expected accounted for 120,000 bpd of the 170,000 bpd jump in the fourth quarter, while strong transportation demand made up 50,000 bpd of the increase.
At the same time, U.S. distillate production at an estimated 3.6 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter was 240,000 bpd higher than EIA previously forecast.
Despite the strong production, stocks failed to build as projected because imports were lower than anticipated.
EIA therefore lowered its projection for distillate stocks at the end of the first quarter by 3 million barrels to 85 million barrels.
The outlook assumed U.S. crude import prices would average $21.04 per barrel, U.S. gross domestic product would grow 2.2 percent, and weather patterns would be normal in 1997.
